title: Claude refusal fallback: a call whose tool_result_meta entry states no kind ran; confine the unanchored "requested permissions" match
outcome: A Claude Bash command that ran and failed is never recorded as abandoned merely because its output mentions refusal-like wording: the refusal-wording fallback applies only where the CLI says nothing about whether the call ran, and the wording table is the single source of that fallback.
acceptance: When a call's tool_result_meta entry exists without non_execution_kind and without a reject permission_decision, the call counts as having run: a behavioural test shows a Bash result 'Exit code 101' whose output contains 'requested permissions', with an entry carrying only its id, is recorded as a finished command, not abandoned.

The unanchored contains("requested permissions") in is_permission_denial is removed or confined to results with no tool_result_meta entry, and CLAUDE_REFUSAL_WORDING alone decides the fallback; existing refusal-signal and unadmitted-denial tests stay green.
The independent review pair has no outstanding Medium-or-higher finding and the full gate passes on the landing input.
